title: BEYOND MEAN FOILS: AUDITING WORST-FOIL SPECIFICITY IN FROZEN CLIP REGION EXPLANATIONS
abstract: Spatial overlap and mean class contrast need not imply target-specific region responses. We audit CCI's maximum-target-drop region in frozen CLIP, using separate prompts for selection and evaluation. Across COCO and VOC with two checkpoints, 41.08-64.78% of locality/mean-foil screen-passers fail a worst-foil criterion. With original screening memberships retained, excluding annotated-present foils leaves 39.69-63.64% failing. Exclusion reduces failure beyond exact cardinality-matched random removal by 0.86-0.92 percentage points on COCO; VOC intervals include zero. Positive-target filtering retains high failure. Among screened failures, unrestricted eight-region oracles permit sign repair in 6.25-7.84% on COCO and 27.40-31.15% on VOC. A target-drop tolerance of epsilon = 0.02 reduces feasible repair to 0.16-0.98%; relaxing it increases opportunity with setting-dependent target and locality changes.
